type: phase-correlated run round — (k,F)=(0,0) closed; ledgers unchanged
headline: Under NR6, no superpermutation of length <= 871 has (k,F) = (0,0). Equivalently every NR6 walk with F = 0 and O = 24 has L >= 872.

s1_run_definition.run: maximal consecutive segment of entries from one E-orbit
s1_run_definition.forced_inside_a_run: a tau step is phase +1 and costs 0; any other intra-orbit step (W3a = phase +2, or a heavy intra-orbit joint) costs >= 1

s2_r_and_splitting.extra_runs: e = r - 24 = sum over orbits of (t_q - 1)
s2_r_and_splitting.fact: t_q = 1 forces m = 5 (the run covers all five phases); t_q >= 2 makes every run of that orbit short

s3_s4_light_move_recheck.W3b: NEVER usable at (0,0), for ANY run endpoint: orb(W3b(v)) always shares a hexagon with orb(v) (720/720) while the cover's 24 orbits are pairwise hexagon-disjoint. The argument does not depend on run length, so it survives outside the r=24 scope.
s3_s4_light_move_recheck.W3a: stays in the same E-orbit (phase +2), so by the definition of a run it is an INTRA-run arc, never an inter-run connector — but at a SHORT run end its target phase can be unvisited, so unlike the r=24 case it is legal. It is therefore admitted into the model and charged to x.
s3_s4_light_move_recheck.conclusion: the unique light INTER-run connector is W3c, for every run length

s9_s10_cost_accounting.identity: S = (r-1) + x exactly; free arcs are exactly the intra-run tau arcs

s7_M_star.definition: M*(B) = max number of DISTINCT E-orbits one all-light chain can cover with combined budget B = (extra runs charged to the chain) + (non-free intra-run arcs in the chain), under exact phase consistency
model_is_an_over_approximation: a run may leave its orbit's phases in any order (any non-tau step charged only 1, although a heavy one really costs >= 2)
hexagon-disjointness is enforced only within the chain, not across chains
s7_M_star.symmetry_used: the S6 relabelling action commutes with sigma, tau and W3c and is transitive on the 720 words, so one starting word suffices (verified: different starts give identical M*)

s8_allocation.budget_accounting: per-chain charges telescope exactly to e + x with no double counting: an orbit appearing in c chains with a_1..a_c runs is charged sum(a_i - 1) + (c - 1) = t_q - 1
s8_allocation.covering: every one of the 24 orbits appears in some chain, so 24 <= sum d_i <= 3B + 4t
s8_allocation.consequence: t >= (24 - 3B)/4, hence B + t >= (24 + B)/4 >= 6 for every B >= 0

theorem.statement: For (k,F) = (0,0): e + x + t >= 6, hence cost = S + H >= 28, hence L >= 872
theorem.scope: conditional on NR6; one of the 55 outer (k,F) cells
theorem.significance: this is the cell in which a length-867 walk (the Houston bound) would have to live; it is now excluded for every length <= 871

s12_positive_control.tightness: B + t = 6 exactly, the extremal case of the theorem

s13_counterexample_search.result: none exists — the theorem forbids them
s13_counterexample_search.note: the bound is attained (B + t = 6) but never violated; the search that established M*(B) = 3B + 4 is exhaustive with no node-cap hits

disclaimer: This project has not proved L6 >= 872. NR6 remains a separate assumption and 54 of the 55 outer cells are untouched.
